sourceFacts.fact: Guillain–Barré syndrome causes peripheral nerve dysfunction with often symmetric weakness.
Weakness commonly begins in the legs and can progress upward.

invariants: Body maps show a common possible pattern; timing and extent vary, no inevitable sequence.
Bilateral/symmetric distribution; no spinal or cerebral lesion depicted.
expectedLabels: Usually symmetric • pattern and progression vary
layoutSpecification: Three small simple front-view clothed child silhouettes from left to right, same scale, neutral stance, no distress. Heading 'A common pattern' under title 'Guillain–Barré syndrome'. First silhouette bilateral feet/lower legs shaded teal; second shading extends to bilateral thighs; third both legs and lower trunk shaded with pale teal extending toward arms. Soft upward arrow BESIDE sequence labelled 'Weakness may ascend'. Small lower line 'Usually symmetric • pattern and progression vary'. No lesion in brain, no spinal cord compression, no reflex hammer or numerical timeline. Diagram conveys possible spread, not an inevitable stage sequence.
